name: application-cookie-preference-center
title: Cookie Preference Center
description: Categorized cookie-consent panel: a locked 'Necessary' row always on, plus toggleable categories with labels and descriptions, and footer Save preferences / Accept all actions.
useWhen: Offering granular, per-category cookie consent (e.g. GDPR/CCPA compliance) beyond a single accept/reject choice.
Users need to understand what each category does before deciding, via a short description per row.
Distinct from a cookie consent banner, which is a single dismissible bar with accept/reject and no per-category detail.
avoidWhen: Your compliance requirements only need a single accept/reject choice with no categories — a simple banner is sufficient and less friction.
The preferences need to live inline in account settings rather than a standalone panel — reuse Preference Toggle Row directly instead.
responsiveBehavior: The panel is a fixed-width card with each category as a single row; footer actions split evenly and remain full-width down to narrow viewports.
accessibility: The Necessary category's switch is a non-interactive <span>, not a disabled <input>, so it's never reachable by keyboard, matching its always-on nature.
Toggleable categories use a real <label htmlFor>/<input type="checkbox"> pair so clicking the label text also toggles the switch.
Each category pairs a short description with its label, so consent decisions aren't made on a bare category name alone.

variants.title: Cookie Preference Center
variants.description: Four categories: locked always-on Necessary, Analytics (on), Marketing (off), and Personalization (off), with Save preferences and Accept all footer actions.
accessibility: The Necessary row's lock state is conveyed by both a non-interactive switch and reduced-opacity styling, not opacity alone.

variants.title: Cookie Preference Center (Dark)
variants.description: The same four-category consent panel adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Switch on/off states and locked-row muting remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
